To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) a 1-band model is sufficient for a qualitative description of the cuprates, and (b) the model is derived from the CuO2 Hamiltonian, and is therefore physically motivated.

(1) the CuO2 plane is described by an effective 1-band Hubbard model; (2) the model is solved by the variational method; (3) the variational parameters are the density of local pairs and the checkerboard density; (4) the variational method predicts a phase diagram with a rich variety of phases; (5) the phase diagram is in good agreement with experimental data.

the cuprate superconductor is described by an effective 1-band Hubbard model, with an effective hopping integral of the same order as the Hubbard U, and with a large effective on-site Coulomb repulsion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic structure and the electronic phase diagram of the high-temperature cuprate superconducting materials.
the physics of strongly correlated electrons in condensed matter.
the electronic structure of strongly correlated electron systems, with particular emphasis on high-Tc superconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cuprates are not superconducting, but are antiferromagnetic, with a small admixture of local pairs, in the sense that the superconducting order parameter is small.
the cuprate superconductor is a strongly correlated system with a very rich phenomenology.
the CuO2 plane has a unique combination of properties which makes it the ideal material for high temperature superconductivity, in spite of its apparent simplicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cuprate high Tc superconductivity can be understood as a consequence of strong electron correlations, which are not only local but extend in space.
the CuO2 layers are the most interesting and the most complicated of the cuprate compounds, because of the strong electron-phonon interaction.
the cuprates can be viewed as a 1-band model of electrons on copper sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to common wisdom, the CuO2 layers are not just a collection of weakly coupled CuO4 plaquettes, but a single entity, a 2D lattice with a very strong coupling between the plaquettes.
the CuO2 plane can be viewed as a 2-dimensional array of quantum dots.
the copper-oxygen planes are special because of their geometry.
